notes.front: What is the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: AWS guidance organised into six pillars that you build into your architecture to produce stable and efficient systems.
notes.explanation: Neglecting the pillars makes it hard to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements.
notes.example: Like a building inspector’s checklist for foundations, wiring and fire safety, but for a cloud workload.
notes.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, “The pillars of the framework”
notes.evidence: When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements. Incorporating these pillars into your architecture will help you produce stable and efficient systems.

notes.front: What is the operational excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar about a commitment to build software correctly while consistently delivering a great customer experience.
notes.explanation: Its best practices reach beyond the workload to how you organise the team that runs it.
notes.example: Like a restaurant that writes down how the kitchen runs, reviews each busy night and improves the routine, rather than only buying better ovens.
notes.evidence: Operational excellence (OE) is a commitment to build software correctly while consistently delivering a great customer experience. The operational excellence pillar contains best practices for organizing your team, designing your workload, operating it at scale, and evolving it over time.

notes.front: What is the security pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar covering the ability to protect data, systems and assets.
notes.explanation: Like every pillar, it gives an overview of design principles, best practices and questions.
notes.example: Like the part of a building code that covers locks, alarms and who holds the keys, but for data and systems.
notes.evidence: The Security pillar encompasses the ability to protect data, systems, and assets to take advantage of cloud technologies to improve your security. The security pillar provides an overview of design principles, best practices, and questions.

notes.front: What is the reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar about a workload’s ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when it is expected to.
notes.explanation: The framework measures reliability against expectations: the right result, every time the workload is needed.
notes.example: Like a train timetable that is only worth having if the trains run correctly and on time whenever they are scheduled.
notes.evidence: The Reliability pillar encompasses the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when it’s expected to.

notes.front: What is the performance efficiency pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar about using cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements.
notes.explanation: The framework adds a time dimension: efficiency has to be kept up as conditions change.
notes.example: Like choosing the right size of lorry for each delivery so parcels arrive on time without wasted space, and changing lorries as orders grow.
notes.evidence: The performance efficiency pillar includes the ability to use cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, and to maintain that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.

notes.front: What is the cost optimization pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar about running systems that deliver business value at the lowest price point.
notes.explanation: Like the other pillars, it offers design principles, best practices and questions, with deeper guidance in its own whitepaper.
notes.example: Like a household that keeps the same comforts but switches to a cheaper energy tariff and turns off lights in empty rooms.
notes.evidence: The Cost Optimization pillar includes the ability to run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point. The cost optimization pillar provides an overview of design principles, best practices, and questions.

notes.front: What is the sustainability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The pillar concerned with reducing the environmental impact of workloads, above all their energy consumption.
notes.explanation: Energy consumption and efficiency are singled out because they are important levers for architects to reduce resource usage.
notes.example: Like a factory that measures the power each machine draws and switches off the idle ones, but for cloud workloads.
notes.evidence: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency, since they are important levers for architects to inform direct action to reduce resource usage.

notes.front: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
notes.back: A no-charge console tool: you define a workload, answer questions on the six pillars, and get a plan built on best practices.
notes.explanation: It is available in the AWS Management Console at no charge, so a review needs no separate purchase.
notes.example: Like a health questionnaire at a pharmacy that produces a personal action plan, but for one workload’s architecture.
notes.source: Overview of Amazon Web Services, “Management and governance: AWS Well-Architected Tool”
notes.evidence: To use the AWS WA Tool, available in the AWS Management Console at no charge, just define your workload and answer a set of questions regarding operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. The AWS WA Tool then provides a plan on how to architect for the cloud using established best practices.

notes.front: How many pillars does the AWS Well-Architected Framework have?
notes.back: Six.
notes.explanation: They are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.
notes.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, “The pillars of the framework”
notes.evidence: When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements.

notes.front: The framework compares a software system to a building: if the {{c1::foundation}} is not solid, structural problems can undermine it.
notes.explanation: In the analogy, neglecting the six pillars is building on a weak foundation.
notes.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, “The pillars of the framework”
notes.evidence: Creating a software system is a lot like constructing a building. If the foundation is not solid, structural problems can undermine the integrity and function of the building. When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars

notes.front: Once the pillars are built into your architecture, what does the framework say you can focus on?
notes.back: The other aspects of design, such as functional requirements.
notes.explanation: Stable and efficient systems from the pillars leave the design effort free for what the system must actually do.
notes.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, “The pillars of the framework”
notes.evidence: Incorporating these pillars into your architecture will help you produce stable and efficient systems. This will allow you to focus on the other aspects of design, such as functional requirements.

notes.front: Operational excellence best practices cover organising your team, designing your workload, operating it at scale and {{c1::evolving it over time}}.
notes.explanation: The pillar covers the people who run the workload and its whole life, not just its first design.
notes.evidence: The operational excellence pillar contains best practices for organizing your team, designing your workload, operating it at scale, and evolving it over time.

notes.front: The security pillar protects data, systems and assets in a way that takes advantage of {{c1::cloud technologies}} to improve your security.
notes.explanation: The pillar treats the cloud as a means of improving security, not only as something that has to be protected.
notes.evidence: The Security pillar encompasses the ability to protect data, systems, and assets to take advantage of cloud technologies to improve your security.

notes.front: Reliability includes the ability to operate and test the workload through its {{c1::total lifecycle}}.
notes.explanation: A workload that works on launch day but cannot be operated and tested later does not meet the pillar.
notes.evidence: This includes the ability to operate and test the workload through its total lifecycle.

notes.front: The performance efficiency pillar includes maintaining efficiency as {{c1::demand changes and technologies evolve}}.
notes.explanation: Meeting today’s performance requirements is only half of the pillar; staying efficient as conditions move is the other half.
notes.evidence: the ability to use cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, and to maintain that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.

notes.front: The cost optimization pillar is about running systems that deliver business value at the {{c1::lowest price point}}.
notes.explanation: The measure is the business value delivered, set against its price, not spending as such.
notes.evidence: The Cost Optimization pillar includes the ability to run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point.

notes.front: The sustainability pillar focuses on {{c1::environmental impacts}}, especially energy consumption and efficiency.
notes.explanation: Those two are named because architects can act on them directly to reduce resource usage.
notes.evidence: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency, since they are important levers for architects to inform direct action to reduce resource usage.

notes.front: Where do you find prescriptive guidance on implementing a Well-Architected pillar?
notes.back: In that pillar’s own whitepaper, such as the Security Pillar whitepaper.
notes.explanation: The framework’s pillar pages give only an overview of design principles, best practices and questions.
notes.evidence: The security pillar provides an overview of design principles, best practices, and questions. You can find prescriptive guidance on implementation in the Security Pillar whitepaper.

notes.front: What does the Well-Architected design principle "stop guessing your capacity needs" say you can do in the cloud?
notes.back: Use as much or as little capacity as you need, and scale in and out automatically.
notes.explanation: A poor capacity decision at deployment can leave you with expensive idle resources or the performance effects of limited capacity.
notes.evidence: If you make a poor capacity decision when deploying a workload, you might end up sitting on expensive idle resources or dealing with the performance implications of limited capacity. With cloud computing, these problems can go away. You can use as much or as little capacity as you need, and scale in and out automatically.

notes.front: Why can you afford to test at production scale in the cloud?
notes.back: You create the test environment on demand, pay for it only while it runs, and decommission it afterwards.
notes.explanation: That lets you simulate your live environment for a fraction of the cost of testing on premises.
notes.evidence: In the cloud, you can create a production-scale test environment on demand, complete your testing, and then decommission the resources. Because you only pay for the test environment when it's running, you can simulate your live environment for a fraction of the cost of testing on premises.

notes.front: What does the design principle "drive architectures using data" ask you to do?
notes.back: Collect data on how your architectural choices affect the workload’s behaviour, and make fact-based decisions to improve it.
notes.explanation: Because your cloud infrastructure is code, that data can inform architecture choices and improvements over time.
notes.evidence: In the cloud, you can collect data on how your architectural choices affect the behavior of your workload. This lets you make fact-based decisions on how to improve your workload. Your cloud infrastructure is code, so you can use that data to inform your architecture choices and improvements over time.

notes.front: What is a game day, in the Well-Architected general design principles?
notes.back: A regularly scheduled exercise that simulates events in production to test how your architecture and processes perform.
notes.explanation: It shows where improvements can be made and builds the organisation’s experience of dealing with events.
notes.evidence: Test how your architecture and processes perform by regularly scheduling game days to simulate events in production. This will help you understand where improvements can be made and can help develop organizational experience in dealing with events.

notes.front: How does the AWS Well-Architected Tool define a workload?
notes.back: Any set of components that deliver business value, such as an application or a website.
notes.explanation: The workload is the unit the tool reviews and compares with the latest architectural best practices.
notes.source: Overview of Amazon Web Services, “Management and governance: AWS Well-Architected Tool”
notes.evidence: The AWS Well-Architected Tool (AWS WA Tool) helps you review the state of your workloads and compares them to the latest AWS architectural best practices. A workload is defined as any set of components that deliver business value, which could be an application or website.

notes.front: What does the Well-Architected Framework give customers and partners who evaluate architectures?
notes.back: A consistent approach, already used in tens of thousands of workload reviews.
notes.explanation: It also gives guidance for designs that scale with application needs over time.
notes.source: Overview of Amazon Web Services, “Management and governance: AWS Well-Architected Tool”
notes.evidence: The Framework provides a consistent approach for customers and partners to evaluate architectures. It has been used in tens of thousands of workload reviews conducted by the AWS Solutions Architecture team and by customers, and provides guidance to help implement designs that scale with application needs over time.

notes.front: A payments team keeps no written procedures, and each on-call engineer handles incidents differently. Leaders want best practices for organising the team, running the workload at scale and improving it over time. Which pillar should guide them?
notes.back: B: Operational excellence
notes.choices:
A) Reliability
B) Operational excellence
C) Performance efficiency
D) Security
notes.choicesExplained: A is about the workload performing its function correctly and consistently. C is about using resources efficiently for performance. D is about protecting data, systems and assets; the gap here is how the team operates.
notes.explanation: Organising the team, operating at scale and evolving over time are the operational excellence pillar’s own subjects.
notes.evidence: The operational excellence pillar contains best practices for organizing your team, designing your workload, operating it at scale, and evolving it over time.

notes.front: A clinic’s architects review how patient records, the systems holding them and other assets are protected in its cloud workload. Which pillar are they applying?
notes.back: D: Security
notes.choices:
A) Cost optimization
B) Sustainability
C) Reliability
D) Security
notes.choicesExplained: A is about business value at the lowest price point. B is about environmental impact and energy use. C is about the workload working correctly when expected; protection of data and assets is security.
notes.explanation: The security pillar is defined as the ability to protect data, systems and assets.
notes.evidence: The Security pillar encompasses the ability to protect data, systems, and assets to take advantage of cloud technologies to improve your security.

notes.front: An online exam service must return the correct results, every time, during the fixed hours when students sit their papers. Which pillar is most concerned with this?
notes.back: A: Reliability
notes.choices:
A) Reliability
B) Performance efficiency
C) Cost optimization
D) Operational excellence
notes.choicesExplained: B is about using resources efficiently to meet performance requirements. C is about business value at the lowest price point. D is about organising and evolving how the team operates; correct and consistent function when expected is reliability.
notes.explanation: Reliability is a workload’s ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when it is expected to.
notes.evidence: The Reliability pillar encompasses the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when it’s expected to.

notes.front: A video platform meets its response-time targets today, but viewer numbers keep changing and newer, faster resource types keep appearing. The team wants to stay efficient as this happens. Which pillar covers it?
notes.back: C: Performance efficiency
notes.choices:
A) Sustainability
B) Reliability
C) Performance efficiency
D) Security
notes.choicesExplained: A is about environmental impact and energy use. B is about correct and consistent function. D is about protecting data and systems; keeping efficiency as demand and technology change is performance efficiency.
notes.explanation: The performance efficiency pillar includes maintaining efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.
notes.evidence: The performance efficiency pillar includes the ability to use cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, and to maintain that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.

notes.front: A board asks its architects to keep delivering the same business value from a system while paying the lowest price possible for it. Which pillar is the board invoking?
notes.back: A: Cost optimization
notes.choices:
A) Cost optimization
B) Performance efficiency
C) Operational excellence
D) Sustainability
notes.choicesExplained: B is judged against performance requirements, not price. C is about how the team builds and operates. D is about environmental impact; business value at the lowest price point is cost optimization.
notes.explanation: The cost optimization pillar is defined by delivering business value at the lowest price point.
notes.evidence: The Cost Optimization pillar includes the ability to run systems to deliver business value at the lowest price point.

notes.front: A retailer has pledged to cut the energy its cloud workloads consume and wants its architects to reduce resource usage directly. Which pillar does this fall under?
notes.back: C: Sustainability
notes.choices:
A) Reliability
B) Cost optimization
C) Sustainability
D) Operational excellence
notes.choicesExplained: A is about correct, consistent function. B is about business value at the lowest price, which may or may not cut energy. D is about how the team operates; environmental impact and energy use are sustainability.
notes.explanation: The sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency.
notes.evidence: The Sustainability pillar focuses on environmental impacts, especially energy consumption and efficiency, since they are important levers for architects to inform direct action to reduce resource usage.

notes.front: An architect wants to review one workload against current best practices by answering questions on each pillar, get an improvement plan, and pay nothing for the review. What should she use?
notes.back: D: The AWS Well-Architected Tool
notes.choices:
A) A Reserved Instance purchase report
B) License Manager
C) A game day in production
D) The AWS Well-Architected Tool
notes.choicesExplained: A concerns pricing, not architecture. B tracks software licences. C tests how the architecture copes with simulated events but does not produce a best-practice review across the pillars.
notes.explanation: The tool is free in the console: you define the workload, answer questions on the six pillars and get a plan based on best practices.
notes.source: Overview of Amazon Web Services, “Management and governance: AWS Well-Architected Tool”
notes.evidence: To use the AWS WA Tool, available in the AWS Management Console at no charge, just define your workload and answer a set of questions regarding operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.

notes.front: Which of these is not one of the pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: B: Scalability
notes.choices:
A) Sustainability
B) Scalability
C) Operational excellence
D) Cost optimization
notes.choicesExplained: A, C and D are all pillars. The six are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability.
notes.explanation: Scalability matters to several pillars but is not a pillar itself, which makes it a tempting distractor.
notes.source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, “The pillars of the framework”
notes.evidence: When architecting technology solutions, if you neglect the six pillars of operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability, it can become challenging to build a system that delivers on your expectations and requirements.

notes.front: How does the performance efficiency pillar differ from the cost optimization pillar?
notes.back: Performance efficiency: using resources efficiently to meet performance requirements. Cost optimization: delivering business value at the lowest price point.
notes.explanation: Both speak of efficiency, but performance efficiency is judged against performance requirements as demand and technology change.
notes.evidence: The performance efficiency pillar includes the ability to use cloud resources efficiently to meet performance requirements, and to maintain that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve.

notes.front: How does the reliability pillar differ from the performance efficiency pillar?
notes.back: Reliability: the workload performs its intended function correctly and consistently when expected. Performance efficiency: it uses resources efficiently to meet performance requirements.
notes.explanation: Reliability asks whether the workload does the right thing whenever needed, throughout its lifecycle; how efficiently it does so is a separate question.
notes.evidence: The Reliability pillar encompasses the ability of a workload to perform its intended function correctly and consistently when it’s expected to. This includes the ability to operate and test the workload through its total lifecycle.

notes.front: How does the AWS Well-Architected Tool differ from the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
notes.back: The framework is the guidance; the tool is the console service that reviews your workloads against it.
notes.explanation: The tool is based on the framework, which was developed to help architects build secure, high-performing, resilient, efficient and sustainable infrastructure.
notes.source: Overview of Amazon Web Services, “Management and governance: AWS Well-Architected Tool”
notes.evidence: The tool is based on the AWS Well-Architected Framework, developed to help cloud architects build secure, high-performing, resilient, efficient, and sustainable application infrastructure.

notes.front: Besides knowing each Well-Architected pillar, what does the exam guide expect you to identify about them?
notes.back: The differences between the pillars.
notes.explanation: The guide lists this as a separate skill from understanding the pillars themselves, so knowing each definition alone is not enough.
notes.source: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) Exam Guide, “Content Domain 1: Cloud Concepts, Task Statement 1.2”
notes.evidence: Understanding the pillars of the Well-Architected Framework (for example, operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability) + Identifying differences between the pillars of the Well-Architected Framework
